text:
The scoreboard said 6-0, and for once it wasn't exaggerating. UTA took 65 shot attempts to CHI's 42 and carried 3.89 expected goals against 1.69, which gives them an 84 percent share of simulated replays. The game was decided in the second period, when UTA out-chanced CHI 1.96 to 0.43 in expected goals and scored three times.

Dylan Guenther was the center of it. His snap shot on the power play at 16:41 of the first opened the scoring, and Michael Carcone made it 2-0 at 17:21, only 40 seconds later. Nick Schmaltz and Anders Lee added even-strength goals in the second, and Guenther tipped in a power-play goal at 15:28 for 5-0. Daniil But finished it in the third. UTA went 2 for 3 on the power play and won 39 of 54 faceoffs. Clayton Keller picked up two assists and Guenther took first star.

Karel Vejmelka needed to make only 15 saves for the shutout, and CHI's chances were thin enough that his work was fair to call modest. At the other end, Arvid Soderblom allowed 2.1 goals more than the 32 shots against him deserved. Barrett Hayton's 33 percent look in the second was the best chance UTA missed. CHI's only real push came in the third, when it led the expected-goals count 0.76 to 0.38, long after the game was decided.
